subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph boundaries with in-band text chunks, explicit boundary metadata, or an intentionally partial common-case repair?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and this PR uses the right shared boundary, but the near-`maxChars` case cannot be fixed by the current text-only shape without a maintainer choice about delivery limits and seam semantics.

options.title: Require a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt boundary metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split seam metadata through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial text repair
options.body: Maintainers could knowingly land the common-case separator fix while tracking the near-limit boundary as remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has strong history on block-reply coalescing and chunking hardening, making it the best available owner for the delivery-contract choice.
